name: Rioja Alavesa
terms: Denominación de Origen Calificada, a step above DO for regions with a record of consistent quality. Only Rioja and Priorat hold it.
Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Spain's regional wine tier, below DO.
A single-estate wine of high quality. A pago is a vineyard estate.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
In Rioja, a red aged at least two years in barrel and bottle, counted from 1 October of the harvest year.
In Rioja, a red aged at least 36 months, with at least 12 in oak. Whites and rosés need 24 months, with 6 in oak.
In Rioja, a red with at least 24 months in barrel and at least 36 more in bottle.

notes: Rioja reds are led by Tempranillo, a fairly neutral grape often blended with Garnacha and Mazuelo and aged long in oak.
Oak and its pronounced vanilla flavor have long been the region's trademark, though some producers now use less.
Rioja Alta's higher vineyards give brighter fruit and lighter wines in an old-world style, while Rioja Alavesa gives fuller body and higher acidity.
Some white Rioja Reserva and Gran Reserva ages for decades into a highly distinctive, aromatic wine.

blurb.text: One of the three zones of Rioja, the Spanish DOCa, the highest level for a regional appellation in Spain. Many Rioja wines blend fruit from all three zones, though single-zone wines are slowly growing.
